latest.content:

Distil PLC

11 August 2026
Distil plc
("Distil" or "Company")
Notice of AGM; Proposed Capital Reorganisation
Distil plc (AIM:DIS) announces
that its Annual General Meeting ("AGM") will be held at 10.00 a.m. on Thursday 3 September 2026 at the offices of Allenby Capital Limited, 5 St Helen's Place,
London, EC3A 6AB.
Distil further announces that the audit of its financial statements for the year ended 31 March 2026 ("Report & Accounts") is near completion but has yet to be finalised. The Company expects to publish its Report & Accounts before 30 September 2026.
The Notice of AGM and Form of Proxy will be posted to shareholders today. Copies of these documents will shortly be available on the Company's website at
www.distil.uk.com
Capital Reorganisation
Resolutions at the AGM include those to facilitate a capital reorganisation.
Pursuant to the provisions of section 580 of the Act, the Company may not issue shares at an issue price which is less than the nominal value of those shares. The market price for the Company's existing Ordinary Shares is currently below its nominal value.
In order to enable the Company to issue new Ordinary Shares at an issue price which exceeds their nominal value, while maintaining the same number of Ordinary Shares in issue, Shareholders' approval is being sought to undertake the Capital Reorganisation.
The Company is proposing the subdivision and re-designation of the existing Ordinary Shares and an amendment to the Company's articles of association, in order to achieve a reduction in the par value of each existing Ordinary Share.
The Company presently has 2,033,799,769 existing Ordinary Shares in issue, each of which has a nominal value of 0.1 pence.
It is proposed that each of the 2,033,799,769 existing Ordinary Shares will be subdivided into and redesignated as one new Ordinary Share of 0.01p and 1 B Deferred Share of 0.09p.
Existing share certificates will remain valid instruments of title - no replacement share certificates will be issued following the Capital Reorganisation.
CREST accounts of Shareholders will not be credited in respect of any entitlement to new B Deferred Shares, and no share certificates will be issued in respect of the new B Deferred Shares.
Expected timetable
2026
Posting of the Notice of Meeting and the form of proxy 11 August

Annual General Meeting 10.00 a.m. on 3 September
Announcement of the result of the Annual General Meeting 3 September
Last day of dealings in existing Ordinary Shares Close of business 3 September
Record Date for Capital Reorganisation 6.00 p.m. on 3 September
Admission of new Ordinary Shares to trading on AIM 8.00 a.m. on 4 September

latest.title: Board Changes
latest.content:
Today 07:00
RNS Number : 3388M
Distil PLC
15 July 2026
Inside Information
This announcement contains inside information for the purposes of the UK Market Abuse Regulations ('UK MAR'). Upon publication of this announcement, this inside information (as defined in UK MAR) is now considered to be in the public domain. The person responsible for arranging the release of this announcement on behalf of the Company is Mr Don Goulding, Executive Chairman.
Distil plc (the "Company")
BOARD CHANGES
Distil plc (AIM: DIS), the owner of premium drinks brands RedLeg Spiced Rum, Blackwoods Gin and Vodka, and Blavod Black Vodka, is pleased to announce the following proposed Board changes as the Company positions itself for its next phase of growth.
Highlights
·
Don Goulding is retiring as Executive Chairman with effect from 14th August
·
Philip Naughton will assume the position of Non-Executive Chairman with effect from 14th August
·
David Smith will be appointed as CEO with effect from 17th August
·
The Company will also seek to bolster the Board with the appointment of an additional independent non-executive director
Retirement of Don Goulding as Executive Chairman
Don Goulding announces that he will step down from the Board of Distil on 14 August 2026. On his retirement, his position will be split, with Philip Naughton becoming Non-Executive Chairman from 14 August 2026, in addition to the appointment of a full-time CEO, detailed below.
Don is retiring from Distil to focus on existing family projects after 16 years with the Company. Having first joined the Board as a Non-Executive Director in 2010, he subsequently became Chairman before assuming the role of Executive Chairman.
During his tenure, Don has played a pivotal role in shaping Distil's strategy and development. He led the creation of RedLeg Spiced Rum, transforming it into one of the Company's flagship brands, successfully guided the business through the unprecedented challenges of the Covid-19 pandemic, spearheaded the Company's strategic investment in Ardgowan Distillery, and recently secured a significant new production and distribution partnership to support future growth in the UK and international markets.
Appointment of Philip Naughton as Chairman
Philip Naughton will assume the position of Non-Executive Chairman on 14 August 2026, having previously joined the Distil board in February 2026 as a non-executive director (announced 28 January 2026).
Philip has extensive corporate experience within the financial services industry, in particular specialising in compliance and governance. Philip was most recently the CEO of a consulting firm. Under his leadership that firm undertook two successful private equity funding rounds.
Proposed Appointment of David Smith as Chief Executive Officer
The Company is delighted to announce the proposed appointment of David Smith as Chief Executive Officer.
David has over 25 years of drinks experience working for IDV, Diageo, the West Indies Rum Distillery and most recently The Oxford Artisan Distillery. David was initially Executive Chairman and then CEO of Fielden Whisky over a 5 year period, transforming it from a founder-led artisanal distillery to a purpose-led business. Securing two rounds of angel investor funding and then in November 2022, merging the distillery with its grain supply partner to create an entity which secured investment from Diageo via its Distill Ventures investment vehicle.
At Diageo he assisted in the launch of RTDs (Ready to Drinks) and built brands in export markets at the West Indies Rum Distillery. David has also been involved in the 0% ABV category, launching and building new brands in the UK market.
It is proposed that Mr Smith will join the Board, subject to the successful completion of the Company's Nominated Adviser's customary due diligence process. A further announcement regarding Mr Smith's appointment will be made once the due diligence process has been completed.
Don Goulding commented:
"As the market begins to recover following a prolonged period of industry-wide challenges, and with a strong strategic production and distribution partner now in place across the UK and export markets, this is the right time for me to step aside.
The Company is well positioned for its next phase of development, and I am delighted that we are strengthening the leadership team by separating the Executive Chairman role and CEO roles. David brings industry experience and a strong track record of building premium drinks brands, while Philip has already made an excellent contribution since joining the Board earlier this year.
I leave knowing the business has a talented team, a strong portfolio of brands and significant opportunities ahead. I wish everyone at Distil every success for the future."
Philip Naughton commented:
"I have greatly enjoyed getting to know the team since joining the Board in February and am honoured to be taking on the role of Non-Executive Chairman at such an exciting point in the Company's development.
Don has provided exceptional leadership and stewardship over the past 16 years. In particular, over the last year he has successfully guided the Company through a number of significant challenges while laying the foundations for the next stage of growth. On behalf of the Board, I would like to thank him for his dedication, vision and commitment to Distil.
I am also delighted to welcome David Smith to the team. David brings extensive experience of the premium drinks industry, most recently the development and successful sale of the Fielden whisky brand. I look forward to working closely with David and the wider team as we build on Distil's strong foundations to support and deliver the Company's next phase of growth."
David Smith commented:
"I have been aware of Distil for many years and I've always been very impressed by their levels of innovation and the quality of their products. Their portfolio has wide consumer appeal and is positioned well for growth against the current trends around affordability. I'm very excited to build on the great platform that Don and the team have created and to take the business on the next stage of his journey"
Further information in relation to David Bradshaw Smith (aged 58)
In addition to his proposed appointment to the Board, Mr Smith holds or has held the following directorships or partnerships in the past five years:
Previous directorships
Current directorships
Fielden Whisky Limited
Oxford Artisan Distillery Limited
SOTH Founder Company Limited
Save for the information above, there are no further disclosures to be made in accordance with Rule 17, Schedule 2(g) of the AIM Rules for Companies in respect of the appointment.

latest.content:
Today 07:00

Distil PLC
13 July 2026
Inside Information
This announcement contains inside information for the purposes of the UK Market Abuse Regulations ('UK MAR'). Upon publication of this announcement, this inside information (as defined in UK MAR) is now considered to be in the public domain. The person responsible for arranging the release of this announcement on behalf of the Company is Mr Don Goulding, Executive Chairman.
Distil PLC
Appointment of Fortitude Drinks to manage full UK distribution
Distil plc (AIM: DIS), owner of premium drinks brands including RedLeg Spiced Rum, Blackwoods Gin and Vodka, and Blavod Black Vodka, is pleased to make the following announcement:
Highlights
·
Distil is moving its UK distribution to Fortitude Drinks ("Fortitude") commencing August 2026
·
Fortitude's group company ICB Drinks (see below) currently bottles some of Distil's brands. This new relationship with the group is expected to present production, packaging, logistics and warehousing cost savings
·
ICB Drinks recently launched a new £10 million canning line which, together with its experienced in-house development team, will enable Distil to expedite the development of new products, including ready-to-drink (RTD)
·
Further to this agreement, Distil and Fortitude are exploring opportunities to work more closely in relation to export markets. Both parties believe that there is significant untapped export opportunity for Distil's Blavod, RedLeg and Blackwoods Gin and Vodka brands
About Fortitude
Fortitude is part of the wider Fortitude Spirits Group owned by Kliro Capital and comprises Fortitude Drinks UK (distribution), Fortitude Spirits (owned brand management), and ICB Drinks (manufacturing, bottling and canning facilities in Middlesbrough). Its business is designed to meet the diverse needs of its partners, offering everything from bespoke product development to reliable distribution solutions, ensuring each spirit not only meets but exceeds consumer expectations
Fortitude Spirits Group has particular strength in the UK off-trade, a key market for Distil, due to the depth of relationship afforded through contracts it holds to produce own-label spirits products as well as a comprehensive range of premium brands. The Group also has national reach in the UK on-trade and is actively growing this channel across its portfolio.
In addition to distribution, the new partnership with Fortitude Spirits Group offers Distil the opportunity to work more closely with the group in terms of production. ICB Drinks already bottles some of Distil's brands, and it is anticipated that the partnership will unlock cost savings in terms of production, logistics and warehousing.
ICB Drinks also recently launched a new £10 million canning line which, together with its experienced in-house development team, will enable Distil to expedite the development of new products, including ready-to-drink (RTD).
Furthermore, Distil and Fortitude Spirits Group are exploring opportunities to work more closely together in relation to export markets. Further detail about the outcomes of these discussions will be shared as it becomes available.
Distil and Global Brands have mutually agreed to conclude their UK distribution arrangement, with Fortitude taking responsibility for distribution from August 2026. The agreement will conclude amicably, and both parties remain open to opportunities to collaborate in the future.
Commenting on the partnership, Distil Executive Chairman, Don Goulding, said: "We are pleased to have the opportunity to work more closely with the team at Fortitude Spirits Group. Alongside its team we hope to make positive impacts on not just volumes in the UK trade, but also across other areas of the business, including production and logistics, and new product development.
We thank the Global Brands team for its commitment and support throughout the time we have worked together. We have nothing but respect for the business and its team and we wish them every success for the future."
Warren Scott, Chairman Fortitude Spirits Group, commented: "We've enjoyed working with Distil on the production of RedLeg over the last 12 months and are excited to now extend that relationship into distribution. The Distil brands are complementary to our existing portfolio, and we look forward to seeing where we can develop the brand portfolio in both the near and long term both in the UK and Internationally."

Distil PLC
9 July 2026
Ardgowan update
Distil plc (AIM: DIS), owner of premium drinks brands Blackwoods Gin and Vodka, RedLeg Spiced Rum and Blavod Black Vodka, provides an update on developments at Ardgowan Distillery Company Limited (
"Ardgowan"
). Distil previously held a Convertible Loan Note relative to Ardgowan. That CLN converted to equity in Ardgowan as advised on 22 June 2026
Issue of Ardgowan equity
Ardgowan has confirmed that it has raised a total of £1,070,500 of equity by the issue of 42,820 new shares in Ardgowan at an issue price of £25 per share, comprising 9.3 % of Ardgowan's issued share capital.
The issue was made available to Ardgowan's existing shareholders. Given Distil's prioritisation of its cash reserves, the Board of Distil determined not to subscribe for any shares in the offer. As a result, Distil's shareholding in Ardgowan has reduced from 10.5% to c9.6%. Distil continues to hold 48,247 shares in Ardgowan
Reasons for the issue
This raise was conducted by Ardgowan as a part of the wider exercise to simplify its balance sheet, which included the conversion of all Convertible Loan Notes into shares (as detailed in Distil's notification 22 June 2026). Ardgowan has raised this cash to settle other debts within the business, subsequently releasing the next tranche of £2m from the Revolving Credit Facility from Nationwide Building Society (trading as Virgin Money).
This further loan from Virgin Money significantly improves the company's cash runway and allows Ardgowan to continue to lay down valuable malt whisky stocks for ageing.

latest.content:

Distil PLC
("
Distil

Company
")
Completion of Ardgowan CLN conversion
Distil plc (AIM: DIS), owner of premium drinks brands Blackwoods Gin and Vodka, RedLeg Spiced Rum and Blavod Black Vodka, announces that, further to its announcement of 4 June 2026, the conditions precedent to the early conversion of its £3 million convertible loan note in Ardgowan Distillery Company Limited have now been satisfied and the conversion has completed.
Highlights
·
Conversion of Distil's £3 million Convertible Loan Note in Ardgowan Distillery Company Limited (
"Ardgowan"
) into an equity interest representing 10.5% of Ardgowan's current issued share capital
·
Distil to be provided with board representation at Ardgowan
·
Receipt of a cash payment of £395,000
·
With immediate effect, Distil will benefit from a rent credit of up to £170,000 in respect of the Blackwoods Brand Home located at the Ardgowan complex. This equates to approximately three years' rent, providing a significant reduction in Distil's future overhead cash costs
Conversion of the Ardgowan Convertible Loan Note
Further to the Company's announcement of 4 June 2026, the conditions precedent to the early conversion have now been satisfied and, as a result, Distil has today converted (the
"Conversion"
) its £3 million Convertible Loan Note (the
"CLN"
) in Ardgowan Distillery Company Limited (
"Ardgowan"
) into shares in Ardgowan.
Distil has received a payment of £395,000, comprising the £195,000 escrow deposit held under the original CLN agreement and a further £200,000. Distil has also received a waiver of rent with effect from Conversion until the aggregate amount of rent waived reaches £170,000. The waiver relates to the Blackwoods Brand Home located at Ardgowan. Distil currently pays rent of approximately £46,000 per annum, payable monthly and subject to periodic RPI-linked rent reviews.
Shareholding in Ardgowan
Following Conversion, Distil holds 48,247 shares in Ardgowan, representing 10.5% of Ardgowan's issued share capital.
Don Goulding, who currently attends Ardgowan board meetings as an observer, is expected to join the Ardgowan board shortly.
Supplemental Agreement
As previously announced, upon Conversion Distil became a party to a supplemental agreement with certain principal shareholders of Ardgowan, which amends the existing shareholders' agreement entered into in 2021. In addition, Distil holds its shares in Ardgowan subject to Ardgowan's amended articles of association. A summary of the principal provisions of the supplemental agreement and the amended articles is set out below.
Summary of principal provisions
Issue of shares (article 3):
unless otherwise approved by a majority, any allotment, grant or disposal of relevant securities must first be offered to qualifying ordinary shareholders on a pro rata basis. These pre-emption provisions do
not
apply to allotment or issue of any shares issued to new investors for the purpose of raising further funds.
Permitted Transfers (article 5):
the amended articles permit transfers with the prior written consent of a majority and also contain customary exceptions for transfers to family members, family trusts, certain permitted transferees connected with Roland Grain and, subject to notice, certain minor shareholders.
Pre-emption on share transfers (article 6):
subject to certain exceptions, a shareholder wishing to transfer shares must first serve a transfer notice and comply with customary pre-emption procedures. If no price is agreed, the transfer price is determined by reference to the lower of the proposed price and fair value, as determined by the auditors.
Compulsory Transfers (article 7):
if an event of default occurs in relation to a shareholder holding 5% or more of the ordinary shares, the remaining shareholders may serve a default notice, following which those shares become disenfranchised and may be subject to compulsory transfer.
Drag Along (article 8):
if shareholders constituting a majority wish to transfer all of their shares to a third-party purchaser, they may require the remaining shareholders to transfer their shares on the same terms.
Tag Along (article 9):
except in the case of a permitted transfer, no sale or other disposition of shares resulting in a change of control may take place unless approved by a majority and accompanied by a tag-along offer to the remaining shareholders
.
General Meetings (article 10):
the quorum for a general meeting is two or more shareholders together holding not less than 25% of the ordinary shares, present in person, by proxy or by duly appointed corporate representative.
Ardgowan
As previously announced, Ardgowan's board, together with its shareholders, convertible loan note holders and lender, has agreed a range of measures intended to recapitalise Ardgowan's balance sheet.
By recapitalising its balance sheet, and in particular removing the CLNs and anti-dilution provisions, Ardgowan is relieved of c. £14m (including accrued and rolled up interest to maturity) of CLNs and c. £0.6m of annual interest cost.
This simplification of the balance sheet, together with the new shareholders' agreement, will make the business more attractive to prospective investors, facilitating the raising of additional capital to accelerate growth, rather than relying on debt facilities.
Distil believes that this improved position should assist Ardgowan in attracting further investment and supporting future growth, which would be in the interests of Distil as a 10.5% shareholder.
In the current financial year ending 30 June 2026, Ardgowan has
delivered
revenue growth of more than 500
%.
The company has also
expanded
its product portfolio
through the
launch of six new single cask editions
within
its Clydebuilt range.
Since opening
for tours and tastings in August 2025,
the Ardgowan Distillery visitor centre has achieved the highest
traveller ranking on Tripadvisor
among attractions in Inverkip.
Against this background, production continues to be ramped
up to enable
further maturing stock
to
be laid
down
, supported by the
recent connection to the mains power supply
.
Blackwoods
Since opening in February 2026, the Blackwoods Brand Home has received strong visitor feedback and currently holds a 5-star Google rating and a number 4 ranking on Tripadvisor.
The Blackwoods team has also made progress in engaging local tourism bodies and tour operators to increase footfall during the current season and into 2027. The Brand Home offers tours and tastings, cocktail masterclasses and, in due course, a gin school, together with a cocktail bar and retail offering.
The opening of the Blackwoods Brand Home has also given the brand a strong platform from which to engage the on-trade, with listings having been won as a result.
Distil believes the Blackwoods Brand Home provides a strong platform for further brand development over the coming season and beyond.

company_30s.what_they_do: DIS.L runs a niche craft spirits business. It distills premium whiskies, produces small‑batch liqueurs, and sells them through its own branded outlets and partner retailers.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The craft‑spirits market is growing fast, and consumers are willing to pay a premium for unique, locally sourced products. DIS.L’s brands have a loyal following in the UK and are expanding into the EU, giving the company a foothold in a high‑margin niche.
company_30s.current_state: The company has just overhauled its board, added a distribution partner, and launched new product lines. Cash burn is still high and revenue is uneven, but the recent moves suggest the firm is actively trying to turn the business around.

rns_narrative: Board changes and a new UK distribution partner signal a shift in strategy – the company is moving from a small‑scale operation to a more structured supply chain.
Product launches such as the Blackwoods brand and a refreshed packaging line show an effort to broaden appeal and increase shelf presence.
The opening of whiskey tours and an investment in a distillery at Ardgowan aim to create experiential revenue streams and strengthen brand storytelling.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet rebuild – the community is largely silent but a handful of insiders are cautiously optimistic.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: A few posts praise the new board and the fresh distribution deal, arguing the company is finally positioned to scale.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Others point out the lack of clear revenue growth, the high burn rate, and the risk that the new products may not gain traction.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The chatter has moved from outright pessimism to a low‑key hope that the recent changes could unlock value.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends is flat – there is no current public interest, which means a catalyst could catch the market by surprise.

near_term_catalysts: Official launch of the new distribution partnership – a spike in sales volume should follow.
First quarterly sales report from the Blackwoods line – positive numbers would validate the product strategy.
Opening day of the Ardgowan whisky tour – media coverage could raise brand awareness.
Potential funding round or strategic investment announcement – would improve cash flow.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a sudden increase in daily volume that coincides with any of the above events, and watch the price touch the 0.04p level (the lowest point in the last year). A rebound from that support would confirm a mean‑reversion thesis.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the early stages of a recovery after a deep crash. A quick burst of activity is expected once the distribution partner is fully operational. If the price holds above the 0.04p floor for a week, it signals that the capitulation phase is ending.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The stock has fallen far below its recent peak, creating a deep low that historically offers the largest rebounds. If the new distribution deal drives sales and the brand launches perform well, the price could climb to the level it was at a year ago. That would be a 400‑plus percent upside from the current floor.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The company still has a high burn rate and no proven revenue stream from the new products. If the distribution partnership fails or sales lag, the price could stay stuck at the floor or even drop further, eroding the remaining equity.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside: 4× the current price. Potential downside: 75% of the current value if the floor collapses again. The asymmetry is favorable for a contrarian trader who can tolerate a long waiting period.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter when volume spikes after the distribution launch and the price moves above 0.05p. Use a 1:4 risk‑reward stop: set a stop 0.02p below the entry and target 0.20p. Scale in as the price consolidates.
playbook.if_watching: Hold a small position at 0.04p and wait for a volume surge. If the price stays flat for two months, consider exiting to preserve capital.
playbook.if_passing: Not applicable – there are no imminent delisting or bankruptcy signals.

ai_insights.bottom_line: DIS.L sits on a deep low, a new distribution partner and product launches could spark a rebound, and the upside is far greater than the downside, making it a compelling contrarian play if the catalysts materialise.
